drivingQuestion: What makes prayer with the congregation efficacious, and from which verse is it learned?
outcomeNote: the value of communal prayer is established from four sources, R' Yohanan's difficulty about Babylonian longevity is settled, and Rav Hisda's ruling is emended into a workable form

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק לְרַב נַחְמָן: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָתֵי מָר לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא לְצַלּוֹיֵי? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא יָכֵילְנָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִכַּנְפִי לְמָר עַשְׂרָה וְלִיצַלֵּי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טְרִיחָא לִי מִלְּתָא. וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ מָר לִשְׁלוּחָא דְצִבּוּרָא, בְּעִידָּנָא דִּמְצַלֵּי צִבּוּרָא לֵיתֵי וְלוֹדְעֵיהּ לְמָר.
segments.en: As a prelude to another of the statements by Rabbi Yoḥanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai, the Gemara relates the following incident. «Rabbi Yitzḥak said to Rav Naḥman: Why did the Master not come to the synagogue to pray?» Rav Naḥman «said to him: I was» weak and «unable» to come. Rabbi Yitzḥak «said to him: Let the Master gather ten» individuals, a prayer quorum, at your home «and pray.» Rav Naḥman «said to him: It is difficult for me» to impose upon the members of the community to come to my home to pray with me (Sefer Mitzvot Gadol). Rabbi Yitzḥak suggested another option: «The Master should tell the congregation» to send a «messenger when the congregation is praying to come and inform the Master» so you may pray at the same time.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מַאי כּוּלֵּי הַאי? אֲמַר לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
segments.en: Rav Naḥman saw that Rabbi Yitzḥak was struggling to find a way for him to engage in communal prayer. «He asked: What is» the reason for «all this» fuss? Rabbi Yitzḥak «said to him: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:»

segments.he: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי לְךָ ה׳ עֵת רָצוֹן״. אֵימָתַי עֵת רָצוֹן — בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר מִתְפַּלְּלִין.
segments.en: «What is» the meaning of «that which is written: “But as for me, let my prayer be unto You, Lord, in a time of favor;» O God, in the abundance of Your mercy, answer me with the truth of Your salvation” (Psalms 69:14)? It appears that the individual is praying that his prayers will coincide with a special time of Divine favor. «When is a time of favor?» It is «at the time when the congregation is praying.» It is beneficial to pray together with the congregation, for God does not fail to respond to the entreaties of the congregation.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ בְּעֵת רָצוֹן עֲנִיתִיךָ״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said that» the unique quality of communal prayer is derived «from here: “Thus said the Lord, in a time of acceptance I have answered you and on a day of salvation I have aided you”» (Isaiah 49:8).

segments.he: רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״הֶן אֵל כַּבִּיר וְלֹא יִמְאָס״: וּכְתִיב: ״פָּדָה בְשָׁלוֹם נַפְשִׁי מִקְּרָב לִי כִּי בְרַבִּים הָיוּ עִמָּדִי״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Aḥa, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said» that it is derived «from here: “Behold, God is mighty, He despises no one”» (Job 36:5). He adopts an alternative reading of the verse: “Behold, God will not despise” the prayer of “the mighty,” i.e., the community. «And it is written: “He has redeemed my soul in peace so that none came upon me; for there were many with me.» God shall hear and answer them…” (Psalms 55:19–20). This verse teaches that the prayer was answered because there were many with me when it was offered.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹאֵס בִּתְפִלָּתָן שֶׁל רַבִּים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֶן אֵל כַּבִּיר וְלֹא יִמְאָס״, וּכְתִיב: ״פָּדָה בְשָׁלוֹם נַפְשִׁי מִקְּרָב לִי״ וְגוֹ׳, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: כָּל הָעוֹסֵק בְּתוֹרָה וּבִגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים וּמִתְפַּלֵּל עִם הַצִּבּוּר — מַעֲלֶה אֲנִי עָלָיו כְּאִילּוּ פְּדָאַנִי, לִי וּלְבָנַי, מִבֵּין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
segments.en: «That» last proof «was also taught» in a baraita. «Rabbi Natan says: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not despise the prayer of the masses? As it is stated: “Behold, God does not despise the mighty,” and it is written: “He has redeemed my soul in peace so that none came upon me;» for there were many with me.” Rabbi Natan interprets this not as David speaking about himself, but as God speaking to Israel. «The Holy One, Blessed be He, says: Anyone who engages in Torah» study, which is called peace in the verse: “All its ways are peace” (Proverbs 3:17); «and in acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation, I ascribe to him» credit «as if he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations of the world.»

segments.he: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּעִירוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ נִכְנָס שָׁם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל, נִקְרָא ״שָׁכֵן רַע״, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ עַל כָּל שְׁכֵנַי הָרָעִים הַנֹּגְעִים בַּנַּחֲלָה אֲשֶׁר הִנְחַלְתִּי אֶת עַמִּי אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל״. וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁגּוֹרֵם גָּלוּת לוֹ וּלְבָנָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִנְנִי נֹתְשָׁם מֵעַל אַדְמָתָם וְאֶת בֵּית יְהוּדָה אֶתּוֹשׁ מִתּוֹכָם״.
segments.en: Continuing to extol communal prayer, «Reish Lakish said: One who has a synagogue» nearby «in his city but does not enter to pray there is called an evil neighbor, as it is stated: “Thus said the Lord: As for all My evil neighbors who touch My inheritance which I have caused My people Israel to inherit,» behold, I will pluck them up from off their land, and will pluck the house of Judah up from among them” (Jeremiah 12:14). One who only touches, but does not enter the place of prayer, My inheritance, is considered an evil neighbor. «And furthermore,» he is punished in that «he causes himself and his children» to go into «exile, as it is stated: “Behold, I will pluck them up from off their land, and will pluck the house of Judah up from among them.”»

segments.he: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִיכָּא סָבֵי בְּבָבֶל. תְּמַהּ וַאֲמַר: ״לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ יְמֵיכֶם וִימֵי בְנֵיכֶם עַל הָאֲדָמָה״ כְּתִיב, אֲבָל בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ — לָא? כֵּיוָן דְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ מְקַדְּמִי וּמְחַשְּׁכִי לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא, אֲמַר: הַיְינוּ דְּאַהֲנִי לְהוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that when the Sages «told Rabbi Yoḥanan» that «there are elders in Babylonia, he was confounded and said: It is written: “So that your days will be lengthened and the days of your children upon the land» the Lord swore to your forefathers to give to them like the days of heaven on the earth” (Deuteronomy 11:21); lengthened in Eretz Yisrael «but not outside of the Land.» Why then, do the residents of Babylonia live long lives? «When they told him» that the people in Babylonia «go early» in the morning «and go late» in the evening «to the synagogue, he said: That is what was effective for them» in extending their lives.

segments.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ: קַדִּימוּ וְחַשִּׁיכוּ וְעַיִּילוּ לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתוֹרְכוּ חַיֵּי. אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי קְרָא — ״אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם שֹׁמֵעַ לִי לִשְׁקֹד עַל דַּלְתֹתַי יוֹם יוֹם לִשְׁמוֹר מְזוּזֹת פְּתָחָי״, וּכְתִיב בָּתְרֵיהּ: ״כִּי מֹצְאִי מָצָא חַיִּים״.
segments.en: «As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said to his sons: Go early and go late and enter the synagogue, so that your lives will be extended.» And «Rabbi Aḥa, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:» Upon «what verse» is this based? As it is stated: «“Happy is the man who listens to Me, watching daily at My gates, guarding at My door posts”» (Proverbs 8:34). «And» the reward for doing so «is written thereafter: “For whoso finds Me finds life and obtains the favor of the Lord”» (Proverbs 8:35).

segments.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לְעוֹלָם יִכָּנֵס אָדָם שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת. שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ?! אֶלָּא אֵימָא, שִׁיעוּר שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְפַּלֵּל.
segments.en: Based on this verse, «Rav Ḥisda said: A person should always enter two doorways into the synagogue.» This statement is unclear. Immediately, the Gemara asks: «Does it enter your mind» that Rav Ḥisda meant that one should enter «two doorways» literally? What if a synagogue only has a single doorway? Rather, emend his statement and «say» that Rav Ḥisda meant that «one should enter a distance of two doorways» into the synagogue «and then pray.» In entering a distance of two doorways, one fulfills the verse: Guarding at My door posts, in the plural.

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי יצחק לרב נחמן: מאי טעמא לא אתי מר לבי כנישתא לצלויי?
moves.summary: R' Yitzhak asks Rav Nahman why he does not come to the synagogue to pray
moves.about: why Rav Nahman does not come to the synagogue to pray

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לא יכילנא
moves.summary: he answers that he is unable to come
moves.about: he was unable to come, being weak

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לכנפי למר עשרה וליצלי
moves.summary: R' Yitzhak proposes gathering a quorum of ten at his home
moves.about: that he should gather ten men at his home and pray with a quorum there

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: טריחא לי מלתא
moves.summary: he declines: imposing on the community is too burdensome
moves.about: that imposing on the community to come to his home is too burdensome

moves.cueHe: ולימא ליה מר לשלוחא דצבורא
moves.summary: R' Yitzhak offers a third option: have the congregation's messenger tell him when they pray
moves.about: that he should have the congregation's messenger tell him when the congregation is praying, so he can pray then

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה מאי כולי האי?
moves.summary: Rav Nahman asks what all this effort is for
moves.about: why R' Yitzhak is going to such lengths to have him pray with the congregation

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: דאמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי שמעון בן יוחי
moves.summary: he answers by citing R' Yohanan in the name of R' Shimon ben Yohai
moves.about: R' Yohanan's teaching on the time of favour, given as the reason for the effort

moves.cueHe: מאי דכתיב ״ואני תפלתי לך ה׳ עת רצון״
moves.summary: the 'time of favour' of Psalms 69:14 is identified as the hour the congregation prays
moves.about: the verse asking that one's prayer come at a time of favour

moves.cueHe: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא אמר מהכא
moves.summary: an alternative derivation from Isaiah 49:8
moves.about: an alternative prooftext for the efficacy of prayer at a time of favour

moves.cueHe: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא אמר מהכא
moves.summary: a third derivation, from Job 36:5 with Psalms 55:19
moves.about: a third prooftext: God, being mighty, does not despise the prayer of the many

moves.cueHe: תניא נמי הכי
moves.summary: a baraita is brought supporting the last derivation
moves.about: a baraita of R' Natan teaching that God does not despise the prayer of the many

moves.cueHe: מנין שאין הקדוש ברוך הוא מואס בתפלתן של רבים
moves.summary: within the baraita, R' Natan asks whence we know God does not despise the prayer of the many
moves.about: the same verse, cited inside the baraita by its own tanna

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״הן אל כביר ולא ימאס״
moves.summary: the two verses are read as God's promise to credit the communal worshipper with redeeming Him and His children
moves.about: the verse read as God's own speech about those who pray with the congregation

moves.cueHe: אמר ריש לקיש
moves.summary: the converse: one who has a synagogue and does not enter it is an evil neighbour
moves.about: the verse on God's evil neighbours who touch His inheritance and are plucked from their land

moves.cueHe: שנאמר
moves.summary: Jeremiah 12:14 supplies both the title 'evil neighbour' and the punishment of exile
moves.about: one who has a synagogue in his city and does not enter it is the 'evil neighbour' of the verse, and is punished with exile for himself and his children

moves.cueHe: אמרו ליה לרבי יוחנן: איכא סבי בבבל
moves.summary: the Sages report to R' Yohanan that there are long-lived elders in Babylonia
moves.about: the report that there are long-lived elders in Babylonia

moves.cueHe: תמה ואמר
moves.summary: he objects that length of days is promised only upon the land, not outside it
moves.about: how Babylonians can live long lives when length of days is promised only 'upon the land'

moves.cueHe: כיון דאמרי ליה מקדמי ומחשכי לבי כנישתא
moves.summary: they answer that the Babylonians come early and leave late from the synagogue
moves.about: the Babylonians go early and late to the synagogue, which is what earns them their years

moves.cueHe: אמר: היינו דאהני להו
moves.summary: he accepts: that is what availed them
moves.about: accepting that the synagogue practice, not the land, is what lengthens the Babylonians' days

moves.cueHe: דאמר רבי יהושע בן לוי לבניה
moves.summary: his charge to his sons to go early and late to the synagogue confirms the point
moves.about: that they should go early and late to the synagogue so their lives be lengthened

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אחא ברבי חנינא: מאי קרא
moves.summary: he asks which verse grounds the charge
moves.about: which verse grounds the charge to go early and late to the synagogue

moves.cueHe: ״אשרי אדם שמע לי לשקד על דלתתי יום יום״
moves.summary: Proverbs 8:34, with the reward of life in the verse after it
moves.about: the verse praising the man who watches daily at God's gates and guards His doorposts

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חסדא: לעולם יכנס אדם שני פתחים בבית הכנסת
moves.summary: Rav Hisda rules from the verse's plural doorposts that one should enter two doorways
moves.about: the verse's plural 'my doorposts' yields the ruling that one should enter the synagogue two doorways' distance

moves.cueHe: שני פתחים סלקא דעתך?!
moves.summary: the literal reading is impossible — a synagogue may have only one doorway
moves.about: taking 'two doorways' literally is impossible, since a synagogue may have only one

moves.cueHe: אלא אימא, שיעור שני פתחים
moves.summary: his words are emended to mean the distance of two doorways, and only then does one pray
moves.about: his words are corrected to mean the distance of two doorways, after which one prays
